prompt.context_jp: 徹夜に近い作業を経て、山と積まれていたチョコレート箱___すべて出荷準備を整えていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 徹夜に近い作業を経て、山と積まれていたチョコレート箱___すべて出荷準備を整えていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits the discourse here.

feedback.correct_en: The chocolate boxes are the already-established topic of the scene (the whole night's work was about them). は marks this as 'as for the boxes, all of them were ready.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the boxes as new information, but they've been the focus the entire paragraph.

contrast_examples.jp: 箱はすべて準備できた。
contrast_examples.en: As for the boxes, all were ready (topic).

contrast_examples.jp: 箱がすべて準備できた。
contrast_examples.en: The boxes (newly noted) were all ready.

prompt.context_jp: 里中の断りは短く柔らかかったが、森美雪にとってはその一言___胸を締めつけるほど重かった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 森美雪にとってはその一言___胸を締めつけるほど重かった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits here?

feedback.correct_en: が highlights 'that single word' as the specific, newly focused thing that weighed on her — a sensory/emotional discovery clause within a 〜にとっては topic frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'that one word' a competing topic, clashing with the existing topic 美雪にとっては.

contrast_examples.jp: 私には彼の言葉が重かった。
contrast_examples.en: To me, his words weighed heavily (focus on the words).
As for his words, they were heavy (topic).

prompt.context_jp: 好きで派遣を やってる人ばかりではありません みんな 事情___あるんです
prompt.prompt_jp: みんな 事情___あるんです
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: ある introduces 事情 as new information — 'everyone has (their) circumstances.' Existence/possession clauses with ある/いる typically take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply contrast ('as for circumstances...') and sounds unnatural here. を doesn't go with intransitive ある.

contrast_examples.jp: 理由はあるが言えない。
contrast_examples.en: There is a reason (contrastive) but I can't say.

prompt.context_jp: 派遣___ 社員よりも仕事ができちゃ いけないんですか？
prompt.prompt_jp: 派遣___ 社員よりも仕事ができちゃ いけないんですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits Haruko's challenge?

feedback.correct_en: Haruko is making a general claim about the category 'temp workers' — は sets up the topic/contrast against 社員. Classic topicalization + implicit contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 'a temp (specific one)' the newly introduced subject, losing the generic/categorical reading.

contrast_examples.en: Temps (as a category) don't work overtime.

prompt.context_jp: 春子の声___いつもと変わらぬ平坦さで、それがかえって場を凍らせた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 春子の声___いつもと変わらぬ平坦さで、…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator shifts focus to Haruko's voice as topic to comment on it (flat as always). は is natural for this descriptive-topic frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a new discovery/report; the voice isn't being newly introduced here.

contrast_examples.jp: あっ、彼女の声が聞こえる。
contrast_examples.en: Oh, I hear her voice (new perception).

prompt.context_jp: (Asano suddenly notices the mic.)
prompt.prompt_jp: マイク___入ってます…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this urgent realization?

feedback.correct_en: This is a sudden realization — the mic being on is new information just noticed. が marks that discovery.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would sound like introducing the mic as a known topic ('as for the mic...'), losing the shock.

contrast_examples.en: As for the light, I turned it off.

prompt.context_jp: 春子___、被り物を外しもせずに淡々と返金伝票を書き続けている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 春子___、被り物を外しもせずに淡々と返金伝票を書き続けている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits (Haruko alone, among the chaos)?

feedback.correct_en: だけが gives the exhaustive-listing reading: 'Haruko alone (and no one else) kept writing.' This fits the contrast with the panicked others.
feedback.incorrect_en: Plain は wouldn't carry the exhaustive 'only her' meaning. だけは would emphasize 'at least Haruko (as for her alone)' which shifts nuance.

prompt.context_jp: なぜ こんなに売れ残って___の？
prompt.prompt_jp: なぜ こんなに売れ残って___の？
prompt.prompt_en: Which fits in the executive's angry question?

feedback.correct_en: 〜てんの (contracted 〜ているの) is natural colloquial for demanding an explanation in the moment.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜てたの would ask about a past state. 〜てますの is ungrammatical register-mixing.

prompt.context_jp: あんた___ 社員じゃないんだから 責任取る必要はない
prompt.prompt_jp: あんた___ 社員じゃないんだから 責任取る必要はない
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits here?

feedback.correct_en: は gives contrastive-topic reading: 'you (unlike me/employees) are not a company employee.' Shoji is contrasting Haruko with the staff who must take responsibility.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would identify 'you' as new subject in a neutral statement, losing the contrast essential to this line.

prompt.context_jp: あの人___ 正社員と やり合ってんの聞いて 何か 元気出てきちゃった
prompt.prompt_jp: あの人___ 正社員と やり合ってんの聞いて…
prompt.prompt_en: Which fits here (describing what she was doing)?

feedback.correct_en: Inside the embedded clause 'that she was arguing with the employee,' が marks the subject neutrally. Subordinate clauses typically take が over は.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would try to set a topic inside the subordinate clause, which sounds off here.

contrast_examples.en: I heard that, as for him, he came.

prompt.context_jp: あ～！ ___生まれる～！
prompt.prompt_jp: 赤ちゃん___生まれる～！(implied)
prompt.prompt_en: If specifying 'the baby is coming,' which particle?

feedback.correct_en: Spontaneous occurrence verbs like 生まれる in-the-moment take が — it reports a new event just happening.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would set 'the baby' as a topic, which is odd mid-contraction when the event itself is the news.

contrast_examples.jp: この赤ちゃんは三月生まれです。
contrast_examples.en: This baby was born in March (topic info).

prompt.context_jp: 破水してますね 救急車___来るまで間に合わないので ここで お産します！
prompt.prompt_jp: 救急車___来るまで間に合わないので…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this subordinate clause?

feedback.correct_en: In the 〜まで subordinate clause, が marks the subject of the embedded event ('until the ambulance arrives'). Subordinate clauses prefer が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would try to topicalize across the subordinate boundary, breaking the natural flow.

contrast_examples.en: I'll wait until the bus comes.

prompt.context_jp: (Haruko reveals her real identity.)
prompt.prompt_jp: 助産師の大前春子___す！
prompt.prompt_en: Which fits in this self-identification?

feedback.correct_en: です is the predicate here: '[I] am Haruko Omae, a midwife.' Self-introduction in a dramatic reveal.
feedback.incorrect_en: が/は alone wouldn't form a complete predicate for name-giving. The copula です is required.

prompt.context_jp: 春子の声___、氷のような普段の口調とは似ても似つかぬ温かさを帯びていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 春子の声___、氷のような普段の口調とは似ても似つかぬ温かさを帯びていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: は establishes Haruko's voice as the topic for the narrator to characterize (unusually warm). Perfect for descriptive statements.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be a report of newly perceived information, which doesn't match the reflective narration here.

prompt.context_jp: 善意を装った営業部からの寄せ書きの真意___、春子は最初から見抜いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 寄せ書きの真意___、春子は最初から見抜いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: 見抜く is a transitive verb — Haruko 'saw through' the true intent. を marks that direct object (fronted for emphasis).
feedback.incorrect_en: が/は can't fill the object slot for a transitive verb that already has 春子 as the は-marked topic.

contrast_examples.en: To see through the true intent.

prompt.context_jp: 義理チョコはね 会社の___ですよ！
prompt.prompt_jp: 義理チョコはね 会社の___ですよ！
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the metaphor Shoji uses for obligation chocolate.

feedback.correct_en: 潤滑油 (lubricating oil) is the set metaphor for things that smooth workplace relations — exactly Shoji's point about 500-yen chocolate.
feedback.incorrect_en: 燃料 (fuel) and 原動力 (driving force) would suggest giving energy, not easing friction.

contrast_examples.jp: ユーモアは職場の潤滑油だ。
contrast_examples.en: Humor is the lubricant of the workplace.

prompt.context_jp: Shoji desperately offers to apologize:
prompt.prompt_jp: ___して来ます！ 絶対 関係 修復します！
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the extreme apology action Shoji vows to perform.

feedback.correct_en: 土下座 (prostrating oneself on the ground) is the ultimate groveling apology — fits Shoji's desperation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 正座 is just formal sitting; 会釈 is a slight nod — neither carries the apology weight.

prompt.context_jp: 思いは形にしないと___ません
prompt.prompt_jp: 思いは形にしないと___ません
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb used in the sales pitch.

feedback.correct_en: 届く ('reach') is the chapter-title verb — feelings must take form to 'reach' the other person. It's also the title: 届かない思い.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見える/分かる are weaker — the pitch is about feelings reaching across to the recipient, not merely being visible or understood.

prompt.context_jp: あんたも もっと人間らしい スキルを___たらどうだ？ 気配りとかさ
prompt.prompt_jp: もっと人間らしい スキルを___たらどうだ？
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb for 'acquire/develop skills.'

feedback.correct_en: スキルを身につける is the standard collocation for 'acquire a skill.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 持ち上げる means 'lift up'; 受け取る means 'receive' — neither collocates with スキル in the sense of mastering.

contrast_examples.jp: プレゼントを受け取る。

prompt.context_jp: Shoji vents his frustration:
prompt.prompt_jp: ___な～ おい！ ゆうべ 徹夜で寝てないからだよ
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the casual verb for 'getting irritated.'

feedback.correct_en: イラつく = to get irritated/annoyed. Fits Shoji's frustrated outburst perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: ニヤつく = smirk; もたつく = fumble/be sluggish — neither matches angry irritation.

prompt.context_jp: 福利厚生もボーナスもない派遣に ___なんて間違ってます！
prompt.prompt_jp: 福利厚生もボーナスもない派遣に ___なんて間違ってます！
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb Haruko uses for 'mooch off / sponge off.'

feedback.correct_en: たかる = to sponge/mooch off someone — carries the critical nuance Haruko intends.
feedback.incorrect_en: もらう is neutral 'receive'; 頼む is 'ask' — neither captures the exploitative sense.

prompt.context_jp: あなたの ___は はっきり言って 気持ち悪いんです
prompt.prompt_jp: あなたの ___は はっきり言って 気持ち悪いんです
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the noun meaning 'meddling/busybody behavior.'

feedback.correct_en: おせっかい is unwanted meddling — Haruko's cutting word for Miyuki's over-the-top celebration.
feedback.incorrect_en: 思いやり and 気遣い are positive words for consideration; they wouldn't be called 気持ち悪い.

prompt.context_jp: Haruko mutters to herself in the mirror:
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___したことが
prompt.prompt_en: Complete Haruko's self-chiding phrase.

feedback.correct_en: 私としたことが is a fixed expression meaning 'How could I of all people (do such a thing)' — self-reproach for an uncharacteristic act (working overtime).
feedback.incorrect_en: The particle must be と in this frozen idiom. が/を break the set phrase.

contrast_examples.jp: 私としたことが、鍵を忘れた。
contrast_examples.en: How unlike me — I forgot the key.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼としたことが遅刻だ。

prompt.context_jp: Context: Asano's annual joking reply when accepting obligation chocolate from Shoji.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more like Asano's actual joking reply in the scene?

choices.text: お返しは 3倍返しで お願いします
お返しを3倍にしてください

feedback.correct_en: 3倍返し is the standard Valentine's/White Day idiom. 〜で お願いします is the natural polite framing of a stipulation.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is literal and grammatical but misses the set-phrase 3倍返し and sounds like a plain request rather than the joking convention.

prompt.context_jp: Haruko defending her 'no overtime' stance.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more pointedly natural for Haruko's retort?

choices.text: 社員が手に負えない仕事を 私は定時までに切り上げてます
社員ができない仕事を 私は時間までに終わらせます

feedback.correct_en: 手に負えない (can't handle) and 切り上げる (wrap up) are precise, workplace-flavored expressions that bite. 定時 ('scheduled end time') is also the key workplace term.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is grammatical but flat — generic 'can't do' and 'finish on time' lose the sharpness and the specific 定時 framing central to Haruko's identity.

prompt.context_jp: Haruko's defiant answer when told '派遣が出しゃばるな.'
prompt.prompt_en: Which reply matches Haruko's style of weaponizing polite form?

choices.text: いえ 出しゃばらせていただきます
いえ 出しゃばりますよ

feedback.correct_en: 〜させていただきます turns the humble form into a cool, formally defiant 'I will take the liberty of butting in.' Classic Haruko irony.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is blunt and casual — correct meaning but loses the icy politeness that makes her comeback cutting.

contrast_examples.jp: 説明させていただきます。
contrast_examples.en: I will take the liberty of explaining.

prompt.context_jp: Haruko orders the men out of the delivery room.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural as a sharp, authoritative order in this scene?

choices.text: 男は出てってください
男の方は退室していただけますか

feedback.correct_en: The contracted 出てって (出て行って) + the blunt topic 男は fits an emergency command — brisk, direct, no-nonsense.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is overly polite office-speak and sounds wrong in a crisis where a midwife is giving orders.

contrast_examples.jp: ご退室いただけますか。
contrast_examples.en: Could you kindly leave the room?

prompt.context_jp: Haruko's cold deflection when told the new product deal is back on.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version matches Haruko's detached, formal brush-off?

choices.text: 私には関わりございません

feedback.correct_en: 関わりございません is stiffly formal (ございません > ありません), perfectly in Haruko's icy-polite register — distancing with keigo.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is colloquial and would sound rude/petulant rather than coolly professional.

contrast_examples.jp: 私には関わりございません。
contrast_examples.en: It is no concern of mine. (formal distancing)
